questions.text: Where do hardwoods come from?
questions.solution: Hardwoods come from deciduous, broad-leaved trees such as oak, beech and mahogany
questions.hint: Think of oak: what kind of leaves does an oak tree have?

options: Trees that grow only in the UK
feedback: Coniferous trees give softwoods
That describes a manufactured board such as MDF

questions.text: Which of these is a softwood?
questions.solution: Pine comes from a coniferous tree, so it is a softwood; oak, beech and mahogany are hardwoods
questions.hint: Look for the wood that comes from an evergreen tree with needles

feedback: Oak is a hardwood
Beech is a hardwood
Mahogany is a hardwood

questions.text: Which of these is a manufactured board?
questions.solution: MDF (medium density fibreboard) is a manufactured board made from wood fibres and resin
questions.hint: Look for the material made in a factory from wood fibres and glue

feedback: Oak is a natural hardwood
Pine is a natural softwood
Ash is a natural hardwood

questions.text: What does MDF stand for? Give the full name.
questions.solution: MDF stands for medium density fibreboard
questions.hint: The F stands for a board made from fibres

questions.text: What is a ferrous metal?
questions.solution: Ferrous metals, such as mild steel and cast iron, contain iron; most of them rust and are magnetic
questions.hint: The word comes from the Latin 'ferrum'

options: A metal that contains no iron
A mixture of a metal and a plastic
feedback: That is a non-ferrous metal, such as copper or aluminium

questions.text: What is the name for a mixture of a metal with at least one other element, such as brass or steel? Give the term.
questions.solution: An alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements, such as brass (copper and zinc)
questions.hint: Mixing metals often makes them stronger or harder than the pure metal

questions.text: Which type of plastic can be reheated and reshaped many times?
questions.solution: Thermoplastics such as acrylic soften when heated and can be reshaped again and again
questions.hint: The name starts with 'thermo', meaning heat

feedback: Thermosetting plastics set permanently and cannot be reshaped

questions.text: Which property describes how easily a material can be drawn out into a thin wire?
questions.solution: Ductility is the ability to be drawn or stretched into a wire; copper is very ductile
questions.hint: Think about how electrical wires are made

feedback: Malleability is being shaped by hammering or pressing without cracking
Hardness is resistance to scratching and wear

questions.text: Which property describes resistance to scratching, cutting and wear?
questions.solution: Hardness is the ability to resist scratching, cutting, indentation and wear
questions.hint: Think about a material that a knife cannot scratch

feedback: Toughness is absorbing impact without breaking
Elasticity is returning to shape after being stretched

questions.text: Name the property that lets a material absorb a sudden impact without breaking.
questions.solution: Toughness is the ability to absorb a sudden shock or impact without breaking
questions.hint: It is the opposite of brittleness

feedback.hardness: Hardness is resistance to scratching and wear

questions.text: Which of these is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.solution: Urea formaldehyde is a thermosetting plastic used for electrical fittings
questions.hint: Thermosetting plastics are often used for electrical fittings and pan handles

feedback: Acrylic is a thermoplastic
Polypropylene is a thermoplastic
HIPS is a thermoplastic used for vacuum forming

questions.text: Brass is an alloy of copper and which other metal?
questions.solution: Brass is copper and zinc; bronze is copper and tin
questions.hint: Bronze is copper and tin, so brass must be different

feedback: Copper and tin make bronze

questions.text: Which of these is a natural fibre that comes from an animal?
questions.solution: Wool comes from sheep (an animal); cotton comes from a plant; polyester and nylon are synthetic
questions.hint: Think about which fibre comes from sheep

feedback: Cotton is natural, but it comes from a plant
Polyester is a synthetic fibre

questions.text: Which natural fibre comes from the seed pods of a plant and is used for jeans and T-shirts? Give the fibre.
questions.solution: Cotton comes from the fluffy seed pods (bolls) of the cotton plant
questions.hint: Denim is woven from this plant fibre

questions.text: A designer needs a lightweight metal that resists corrosion for drinks cans. Which metal is most suitable?
questions.solution: Aluminium is lightweight and resists corrosion, so it is used for drinks cans
questions.hint: Which metal is light and does not rust?

feedback: Lead is very heavy and toxic
Mild steel is heavier and rusts unless coated

questions.text: Which smart material changes colour when its temperature changes?
questions.solution: Thermochromic pigments change colour with temperature, as in colour-changing mugs and baby spoons
questions.hint: 'Thermo' means heat and 'chromic' means colour

feedback: Photochromic pigments respond to light, not heat

questions.text: Sunglasses that darken in bright sunlight use which type of smart material? Give the term.
questions.solution: Photochromic materials change colour when exposed to light (UV)
questions.hint: 'Photo' means light and 'chromic' means colour

feedback.thermochromic: Thermochromic materials respond to temperature, not light

questions.text: Which pair of properties makes copper suitable for electrical wires?
questions.solution: Copper conducts electricity very well and is ductile, so it can be drawn into wires
questions.hint: Electricity must flow through it, and it must be stretched into wire

feedback: An insulator would stop the current flowing

questions.text: A chair seat has a built-in 'living hinge' that can bend thousands of times without breaking. Which plastic is it most likely made from?
questions.solution: Polypropylene resists fatigue, so it is used for living hinges such as on lunch boxes and bottle caps
questions.hint: The plastic is tough and flexible, unlike a brittle one

feedback: Acrylic is brittle and would crack
Urea formaldehyde is a rigid thermoset

questions.text: Which manufactured board is made by gluing thin layers of wood veneer with the grain of each layer at 90° to the next? Give the name.
questions.solution: Plywood is made from layers (plies) of veneer glued with the grain at 90°, making it strong
questions.hint: Each thin layer is called a ply

questions.text: Which of these is a composite material?
questions.solution: GRP combines glass fibres and resin, so it is a composite
questions.hint: A composite combines two or more different materials to get better properties

feedback: Mild steel is an alloy (iron and carbon), not a composite

questions.text: A racing bike frame must be stiff, strong and very light. Which material is best suited?
questions.solution: Carbon fibre reinforced plastic has a very high strength-to-weight ratio, so it suits racing bikes
questions.hint: Look for the composite with a very high strength-to-weight ratio

feedback: Cast iron is heavy and brittle
LDPE is soft and flexible

questions.text: Why are oak garden benches usually fixed with brass or stainless steel screws instead of plain steel screws?
questions.solution: Oak contains tannic acid, which corrodes plain steel and causes black stains; outdoors, steel would also rust
questions.hint: Think about what oak contains and what happens to steel outside

options: Acid in oak corrodes plain steel, and plain steel would rust outdoors
Oak is too soft to hold steel screws
Steel screws are not strong enough for wood
Brass is magnetic and grips the wood better
feedback: Brass is not magnetic

questions.text: Mild steel is cheap and strong but rusts easily. Which finish coats it with zinc by dipping it in molten zinc?
questions.solution: Galvanising coats steel with zinc, which protects it from rusting
questions.hint: The name comes from the scientist Galvani

feedback: Anodising is used on aluminium
Varnish is mainly used on wood

questions.text: A shape memory alloy returns to its original shape when heated. Give the trade name of the common nickel–titanium shape memory alloy.
questions.solution: Nitinol is a nickel–titanium alloy used in glasses frames and medical stents
questions.hint: Its name is made from the letters of nickel, titanium and the place where it was developed

questions.text: In a test, a material snaps cleanly under a sharp knock without bending first. Which property is it showing?
questions.solution: A material that breaks suddenly without bending is brittle, like glass or cast iron
questions.hint: Think of glass breaking

feedback: A tough material would absorb the knock without breaking

questions.text: Which manufactured board is made from wood chips bonded with resin and is often covered with a veneer or laminate for kitchen units?
questions.solution: Chipboard is made from wood chips and resin; it is cheap and usually covered with a veneer or laminate
questions.hint: The name tells you what it is made from

feedback: Plywood is made from layers of veneer
MDF is made from fine wood fibres

questions.text: Steel is mainly iron mixed with a small amount of which non-metal element? Give the element.
questions.solution: Steel is an alloy of iron and a small amount of carbon
questions.hint: The same element is found in charcoal and diamonds

questions.text: Which statement about softwoods and hardwoods is accurate?
questions.solution: Hardwood and softwood describe the tree type (deciduous or coniferous), not hardness: balsa is a soft hardwood
questions.hint: Remember that the classification is based on the tree, not on how hard the wood feels

options: The names describe the type of tree, so balsa is a hardwood even though it is very soft
Hardwoods are always harder than softwoods
Balsa is a softwood, being easy to cut
feedback: Balsa is a hardwood but is very soft
Softwoods come from coniferous trees

questions.text: Why is a thermosetting plastic such as melamine formaldehyde used for kitchen worktop laminates instead of a thermoplastic?
questions.solution: Thermosets have cross-links that stop them softening when reheated, so they resist heat from hot pans
questions.hint: Think about what happens when a hot pan is put on the surface

options: Thermosets can be melted and recycled easily
Thermosets do not soften when heated again, so hot pans will not damage them
Thermosets are the cheapest plastics and bend easily
feedback: Thermosets cannot be remelted

questions.text: Why is cast iron suitable for the heavy base of a machine vice but not for the head of a hammer?
questions.solution: Cast iron is hard and strong in compression, but brittle, so it can crack under sharp impacts
questions.hint: Compare a part that just sits under load with a part that is hit again and again

options: Cast iron is too soft to be used as a hammer
Cast iron is too light for a hammer head
Cast iron is strong in compression but brittle, so a hammer head could crack under repeated impacts
Cast iron melts when it is hit
feedback: Cast iron is hard; the problem is that it is brittle

questions.text: Which statement about stainless steel is accurate?
questions.solution: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron, carbon and chromium (often with nickel); the chromium resists corrosion
questions.hint: Think about why cutlery and sinks do not rust

options: Stainless steel is a pure metal with no iron
Stainless steel rusts more easily than mild steel
Stainless steel is an alloy containing chromium, which helps it resist corrosion
feedback: Steel is mostly iron, so stainless steel is a ferrous alloy

questions.text: Which modern material is a single layer of carbon atoms, extremely strong and an excellent conductor? Give the name.
questions.solution: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms in a hexagonal lattice
questions.hint: Its name is related to graphite, the 'lead' in pencils

questions.text: Sportswear must stretch and then recover its shape. Which fibre is usually added to give this property?
questions.solution: Elastane (often sold as Lycra) can stretch to several times its length and recover its shape
questions.hint: The fibre's name sounds like the property you need

feedback: Linen is strong but creases and does not stretch much

questions.text: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.solution: Wind will not run out, so it is renewable; coal, oil and natural gas are fossil fuels
questions.hint: Which one will never run out?

feedback: Coal is a fossil fuel and will run out
Oil is a fossil fuel and will run out

questions.text: What are the three main blocks of a systems diagram?
questions.solution: A system diagram shows input → process → output
questions.hint: Think of a switch, a control circuit and a buzzer

questions.text: What type of motion is movement in a straight line in one direction? Give the term.
questions.solution: Movement in a straight line in one direction is linear motion
questions.hint: The word comes from 'line'

questions.text: What type of motion is swinging backwards and forwards in an arc, like a pendulum?
questions.solution: Swinging back and forth in an arc is oscillating motion
questions.hint: Think of a clock pendulum or a swing

feedback: Reciprocating is backwards and forwards in a straight line

questions.text: What type of motion is turning in a circle, like a wheel? Give the term.
questions.solution: Turning in a circle is rotary motion
questions.hint: Think of something that rotates

questions.text: What is the name of the point that a lever pivots around? Give the term.
questions.solution: A lever turns about its pivot point, called the fulcrum
questions.hint: On a see-saw, it is the point in the middle

feedback.load: The load is the weight being moved
feedback.effort: The effort is the force you apply

questions.text: What does LED stand for? Give the full term.
questions.solution: LED stands for light emitting diode, an output that gives light
questions.hint: The D is a component that lets current flow one way only

questions.text: Which statement about reciprocating and oscillating motion is accurate?
questions.solution: Reciprocating motion moves back and forth in a straight line (a saw); oscillating swings in an arc (a pendulum)
questions.hint: Compare a sewing machine needle with a pendulum

options: Reciprocating is backwards and forwards in an arc; oscillating is backwards and forwards in a straight line
Both mean turning in a full circle
Both mean moving in one direction only
Reciprocating is backwards and forwards in a straight line; oscillating is backwards and forwards in an arc
feedback: Turning in a circle is rotary motion

questions.text: Which of these components is an output device?
questions.solution: A buzzer produces sound, so it is an output; the others are inputs
questions.hint: Outputs do something you can see, hear or feel

feedback: A thermistor senses temperature, so it is an input

questions.text: Name the input component whose resistance changes with temperature.
questions.solution: A thermistor's resistance changes with temperature, so it is used as a temperature sensor
questions.hint: Its name begins with 'therm', meaning heat

questions.text: A wheelbarrow is which class of lever?
questions.solution: In a wheelbarrow the wheel is the fulcrum, the load is in the middle and the effort is at the handles: second class
questions.hint: Find the fulcrum, load and effort: which one is in the middle?

feedback: In a first-class lever the fulcrum is in the middle
In a third-class lever the effort is in the middle

questions.text: Which mechanism changes rotary motion into reciprocating motion?
questions.solution: A rotating cam pushes the follower up and down, changing rotary motion to reciprocating motion
questions.hint: Look for the mechanism that makes something go up and down

feedback: Spur gears change speed, but the motion stays rotary
Bevel gears turn rotary motion through 90°

questions.text: Name the device that stores chemical energy and supplies electrical energy to a portable circuit.
questions.solution: A battery (made of one or more cells) stores chemical energy
questions.hint: Torches and remote controls need one of these

questions.text: Which energy source uses heat from hot rocks deep underground?
questions.solution: Geothermal energy uses heat from rocks deep underground
questions.hint: 'Geo' means Earth and 'thermal' means heat

feedback: Biomass uses plant or animal material as fuel

questions.text: Which arrangement is correctly ordered as input, then process, then output?
questions.solution: The switch is the input, the microcontroller processes the signal and the buzzer is the output
questions.hint: Which component does the user press first?

questions.text: A driver gear with 10 teeth turns a driven gear with 30 teeth. The driver turns at 300 rpm. How fast does the driven gear turn? Give the answer in rpm.
questions.solution: Gear ratio = 30 ÷ 10 = 3, so output speed = 300 ÷ 3 = 100 rpm
questions.hint: Work out the gear ratio (driven teeth ÷ driver teeth) first

mistakes.feedback: A bigger driven gear turns more slowly, so divide by the gear ratio

questions.text: A driver gear has 15 teeth and the driven gear has 45 teeth. What is the gear ratio?
questions.solution: Gear ratio = driven teeth ÷ driver teeth = 45 ÷ 15 = 3, written 3:1
questions.hint: Divide the number of teeth on the driven gear by the number on the driver

feedback: Put the driven gear first: 45 ÷ 15 = 3, so 3:1

questions.text: A lever lifts a 100 N load with a 20 N effort. What is the mechanical advantage?
questions.solution: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 100 ÷ 20 = 5
questions.hint: Divide the load by the effort

feedback: You divided effort by load; it is load ÷ effort
Divide, do not subtract

questions.text: A pair of scissors is which class of lever?
questions.solution: Scissors have the pivot (fulcrum) between the effort at the handles and the load at the blades: first class
questions.hint: Where is the pivot compared with your fingers and the paper?

feedback: In a second-class lever the load is in the middle

questions.text: A light must switch on automatically when it gets dark. Which input sensor is needed?
questions.solution: An LDR's resistance changes with light level, so it can detect darkness
questions.hint: Which sensor responds to light?

feedback: A thermistor senses temperature

questions.text: A wind turbine changes the kinetic energy of the wind into which form of energy? Give the form of energy.
questions.solution: A wind turbine turns kinetic energy into electrical energy using a generator
questions.hint: The turbine drives a generator connected to the grid

questions.text: Which mechanism changes rotary motion into linear motion, as in some car steering systems?
questions.solution: A rack and pinion changes rotary motion (pinion) into linear motion (rack)
questions.hint: One part is a round gear and the other is a straight toothed bar

feedback: A ratchet and pawl lets something turn in one direction only

questions.text: A driver pulley of diameter 50 mm turns a driven pulley of diameter 150 mm. The driver turns at 900 rpm. What is the speed of the driven pulley? Give the answer in rpm.
questions.solution: Ratio = 150 ÷ 50 = 3, so driven speed = 900 ÷ 3 = 300 rpm
questions.hint: Find how many times bigger the driven pulley is first

mistakes.feedback: A bigger driven pulley turns more slowly, so divide by the ratio

questions.text: Why is an idler gear placed between a driver gear and a driven gear?
questions.solution: An idler gear reverses the direction again, so the driven gear turns the same way as the driver; it does not change the ratio
questions.hint: Two meshing gears turn in opposite directions. What happens with three?

options: To double the speed of the driven gear
To change rotary motion into linear motion
To make the driven gear turn in the same direction as the driver
To stop the gears wearing out
feedback: An idler gear does not change the gear ratio

questions.text: Which statement about a worm gear and wheel is accurate?
questions.solution: A worm and wheel gives a very large speed reduction, and the wheel cannot turn the worm, which makes it self-locking
questions.hint: One turn of the worm moves the wheel on by only one tooth

options: The output speed is greatly increased
Rotary motion is changed into reciprocating motion
The wheel always drives the worm
There is a large reduction in speed, and the wheel cannot drive the worm
feedback: A worm gear reduces speed a lot

questions.text: Two pulleys are joined by a crossed belt. What is the effect?
questions.solution: Crossing the belt reverses the direction of the driven pulley
questions.hint: Draw the belt crossing over between the pulleys and follow its direction

options: The driven pulley turns in the opposite direction
The driven pulley turns faster in the same direction
The belt can no longer slip

questions.text: Which linkage changes the direction of motion through 90°?
questions.solution: A bell crank turns the direction of motion through 90°, as in bicycle brakes
questions.hint: This linkage is used to send a brake cable round a corner

feedback: A reverse motion linkage makes the output move in the opposite direction
A parallel motion linkage makes the output move in the same direction

questions.text: Name the cam shape that lets the follower rise slowly and then drop suddenly. Give the name.
questions.solution: A snail (drop) cam gives a slow rise and then a sudden drop
questions.hint: It is named after a garden creature with a spiral shell

questions.text: A driver gear has 12 teeth and the driven gear has 36 teeth. Which statement is accurate?
questions.solution: Gear ratio = 36 ÷ 12 = 3:1, so the driven gear turns at a third of the driver's speed, in the opposite direction
questions.hint: Work out the gear ratio first

options: The driven gear turns three times faster than the driver
Both gears turn in the same direction
The driven gear turns at one third of the driver's speed
The driven gear turns at the same speed as the driver
feedback: Two meshing gears turn in opposite directions

questions.text: Why does a bicycle use a chain and sprockets instead of a belt and pulleys?
questions.solution: Chain and sprocket gives a positive drive that cannot slip, which suits the large forces from pedalling
questions.hint: Think about what could happen to a belt when you pedal hard uphill

options: Chains need no lubrication or maintenance
A chain makes the wheel turn in the opposite direction
Chains are always quieter than belts
The chain cannot slip under heavy loads, so the drive is positive
feedback: Chains need regular oiling

questions.text: Which statement about nuclear power is accurate?
questions.solution: Nuclear power is non-renewable (finite uranium) and low-carbon, but produces radioactive waste
questions.hint: Think about the fuel, the emissions and the waste separately

options: Uranium fuel will run out, so nuclear power is non-renewable, but very little carbon dioxide is released while running
Nuclear power stations release large amounts of carbon dioxide
feedback: Nuclear power produces radioactive waste that must be stored safely

questions.text: Which statement about rechargeable batteries compared with disposable alkaline batteries is accurate?
questions.solution: Rechargeable batteries cost more at first but can be recharged hundreds of times, so less waste is produced
questions.hint: Compare the cost of buying once with the cost over many uses

options: They cost more to buy but can be reused many times, reducing waste
They always have to be thrown away after one use
feedback: All batteries store energy in chemicals

questions.text: Tweezers are a third-class lever. Which statement is accurate?
questions.solution: In a third-class lever the effort is in the middle; the mechanical advantage is less than 1, but movement is precise
questions.hint: Find where you squeeze the tweezers compared with the hinge and the tips

options: The load is between the effort and the fulcrum, giving a large mechanical advantage
The fulcrum is between the effort and the load
The effort is between the fulcrum and the load, so they give control rather than a mechanical advantage
feedback: That is a first-class lever

questions.text: Why might a designer use a solar cell and a rechargeable battery in a garden light?
questions.solution: The solar cell generates electricity in daylight and stores it in the battery for use after dark
questions.hint: When is the light needed, and when is the sun shining?

options: Solar cells produce more energy at night
Solar cells only work with disposable batteries
The solar cell charges the battery in daylight so the light can work at night

questions.text: A system measures its output and uses the result to adjust the process, like a thermostat. Give the term for this.
questions.solution: Feedback (a closed-loop system) uses information about the output to control the process
questions.hint: Information goes back from the output to the process

questions.text: Which scale of production makes a single, unique product for one client?
questions.solution: One-off (bespoke or job) production makes a single unique product, such as a made-to-measure wedding dress
questions.hint: Think of a made-to-measure item

feedback: Batch production makes a set number of identical products

questions.text: What does CAD stand for? Give the full term.
questions.solution: CAD stands for computer aided design
questions.hint: The D is the stage before making

feedback.computer aided manufacture: That is CAM; CAD is the design stage

questions.text: What does CAM stand for? Give the full term.
questions.solution: CAM stands for computer aided manufacture, using machines such as laser cutters
questions.hint: The M is the stage after designing

feedback.computer aided design: That is CAD; CAM is the making stage

questions.text: Name the hand saw with a thin blade in a C-shaped frame, designed for cutting curves in wood and plastic.
questions.solution: A coping saw has a thin blade in a frame, so it can cut curves
questions.hint: Its name begins with 'cop'

feedback.tenon saw: A tenon saw cuts straight lines in wood

questions.text: Which piece of personal protective equipment protects your eyes when using a pillar drill?
questions.solution: Goggles protect the eyes from flying swarf and dust
questions.hint: Which part of the body is named in the question?

questions.text: What is a jig used for?
questions.solution: A jig guides a tool (for example, a drill) so identical parts can be made accurately and quickly
questions.hint: Think about drilling the same hole in 50 identical parts

options: Measuring the temperature of a material
Guiding a tool so the same process can be repeated accurately

questions.text: What does CNC stand for? Give the full term.
questions.solution: CNC stands for computer numerical control: machines follow coded instructions from a computer
questions.hint: The N stands for numbers (coordinates) that control the machine

questions.text: Which statement about batch and mass production is accurate?
questions.solution: Batch production makes a set quantity (such as 100 chairs); mass production makes thousands, often on a production line
questions.hint: Compare a bakery making 200 loaves with a car factory

options: Batch makes one unique product; mass makes a set number of products
Batch makes very large numbers on an assembly line; mass makes a set number
Batch and mass production both make one product at a time by hand
Batch makes a set number of identical products; mass makes very large numbers, often on an assembly line
feedback: One unique product is one-off production

questions.text: Which process heats a thermoplastic sheet and then sucks it down over a mould?
questions.solution: Vacuum forming heats a plastic sheet (often HIPS) and sucks out the air so it forms over a mould
questions.hint: Air is removed from underneath the soft sheet

feedback: Injection moulding forces melted plastic granules into a closed mould

questions.text: Which of these is an additive manufacturing process?
questions.solution: 3D printing builds a product layer by layer, adding material; the others remove material
questions.hint: Additive means building up, not cutting away

feedback: Laser cutting removes material, so it is subtractive

questions.text: Which saw has a fine-toothed blade held in a frame and is used for cutting metal? Give the name.
questions.solution: A hacksaw (or junior hacksaw) is used for cutting metal
questions.hint: Its name starts with 'hack'

questions.text: Which finish colours and protects aluminium by thickening its oxide layer?
questions.solution: Anodising thickens the oxide layer on aluminium and can add colour
questions.hint: This finish is used on coloured aluminium water bottles

feedback: Galvanising coats steel with zinc

questions.text: Which wood joint uses interlocking wedge-shaped tails and pins and is often used for drawers?
questions.solution: A dovetail joint has interlocking tails and pins, so it resists being pulled apart
questions.hint: The shape looks like a bird's tail

feedback: A butt joint is two flat ends glued together, and it is weak

questions.text: Which process forces melted plastic granules into a closed mould under pressure to make complex parts such as toy bricks? Give the process.
questions.solution: Injection moulding forces melted plastic into a mould under high pressure
questions.hint: The plastic is 'injected', like a syringe

feedback.blow moulding: Blow moulding makes hollow shapes such as bottles

questions.text: A part should be 40 mm long with a tolerance of ±0.5 mm. What is the largest acceptable length? Give the answer in mm.
questions.solution: Largest length = 40 + 0.5 = 40.5 mm
questions.hint: The tolerance tells you how far above or below 40 mm is allowed

mistakes.feedback: That is the smallest acceptable length; add the tolerance for the largest

questions.text: A shelf is designed to be 600 mm long with a tolerance of ±2 mm. What is the smallest acceptable length? Give the answer in mm.
questions.solution: Smallest length = 600 − 2 = 598 mm
questions.hint: Subtract the tolerance from the design size

mistakes.feedback: That is the largest acceptable length; subtract for the smallest

questions.text: A school needs 30 identical wooden name plates. Which scale of production is most suitable?
questions.solution: A set number of identical items is batch production
questions.hint: The number of items is fixed and not very large

feedback: Mass production is for thousands of items

questions.text: A designer wants to cut and engrave 50 identical acrylic keyrings accurately. Which machine is most suitable?
questions.solution: A laser cutter (CAM) cuts and engraves sheet materials such as acrylic accurately and repeatedly
questions.hint: Which CAM machine both cuts and engraves sheet material?

feedback: A coping saw is a hand tool, so 50 identical keyrings would be slow and less accurate

questions.text: A plastic drinks bottle with a narrow neck is made by which process?
questions.solution: Blow moulding blows air into a hot plastic tube inside a mould, making hollow shapes such as bottles
questions.hint: Air is blown inside the hot plastic

feedback: Vacuum forming makes open shapes such as trays, not narrow-necked bottles

questions.text: A long plastic pipe with the same cross-section all the way along is made by pushing melted plastic through a shaped die. Give the process.
questions.solution: Extrusion pushes material through a die to make long, constant profiles
questions.hint: Think of squeezing toothpaste out of a tube

questions.text: Which tool is used to mark a line parallel to the edge of a piece of wood?
questions.solution: A marking gauge scratches a line parallel to the edge of the wood
questions.hint: The tool slides along the edge as you mark

feedback: A try square marks lines at 90° to an edge

questions.text: A factory changes from batch to mass production for a popular toy. What is the most likely effect?
questions.solution: Mass production spreads the high set-up cost over many products, so each one costs less
questions.hint: Think about economies of scale

options: A lower cost per toy, but a high set-up cost for tooling and machines
A higher cost per toy and less use of machines
Each toy can be customised for each customer
feedback: Mass production still needs quality control

questions.text: Which is an advantage of using CAM rather than making parts by hand?
questions.solution: CAM machines follow the same file each time, giving accuracy and consistency
questions.hint: Think about making 100 identical parts

options: Identical, accurate parts can be made quickly and repeatedly
CAM is always cheaper for a single one-off product
feedback: CAM needs a CAD file to follow

questions.text: Brackets must be 25 mm ± 0.2 mm long. One bracket measures 25.3 mm. By how many mm is it over the upper limit? Give the answer in mm.
questions.solution: Upper limit = 25 + 0.2 = 25.2 mm; 25.3 − 25.2 = 0.1 mm over
questions.hint: Find the upper limit first

mistakes.feedback: Compare with the upper limit (25.2 mm), not with 25 mm

questions.text: Before drilling a hole in mild steel, which tool makes a small dent so the drill bit does not wander?
questions.solution: A centre punch makes a small dent in metal to locate the drill bit
questions.hint: It is hit with a hammer

feedback: A scriber marks lines on metal
A bradawl starts holes in wood

questions.text: Why is just-in-time (JIT) manufacturing used?
questions.solution: JIT orders materials to arrive just before they are needed, saving storage space and money
questions.hint: Think about what the name says about timing

options: Products are made only by hand
Large stocks are stored in case of delays
Products are made slowly so each one is unique
Materials arrive only when needed, cutting storage costs and waste
feedback: JIT avoids keeping large stocks

questions.text: Give the term for the allowed range of sizes for a part, such as 50 mm ± 1 mm.
questions.solution: A tolerance is the acceptable range of size above and below the design size
questions.hint: It is how much variation you will 'put up with'

questions.text: Which joining process uses a filler metal with a lower melting point than the parts and is used on circuit boards?
questions.solution: Soldering joins components on circuit boards with a low-melting-point filler metal
questions.hint: This process uses an iron and a reel of thin metal wire

feedback: Welding melts the parts themselves together

questions.text: Why is injection moulding suitable for mass production but not for a one-off product?
questions.solution: The high cost of the steel mould is only worth paying when it is spread over thousands of parts
questions.hint: Compare the cost of the mould with the cost of each part

options: The mould can only be used once
The mould is very expensive to make, but each part after that is cheap and quick
Only simple flat shapes can be made
Each part takes several days to cool
feedback: Injection moulding can make very complex shapes

questions.text: Which statement about quality control is accurate?
questions.solution: Quality control inspects and tests products during and after making, often using tolerances
questions.hint: Think about when and how products are inspected

options: Products are only checked once they have been sold
Quality control means the designer approves the first sketch
Products or parts are checked during and after manufacture against set standards
Quality control removes the need for tolerances
feedback: Tolerances are used in quality control checks

questions.text: Why would a maker use a template when cutting out 40 identical wooden shapes?
questions.solution: A template is drawn around to mark the same shape again and again, saving time and improving accuracy
questions.hint: Think about drawing around a stencil

options: To hold the drill at a set angle
To give the wood a waterproof finish
To mark out the same shape quickly and consistently each time
feedback: Guiding a tool is the job of a jig

questions.text: Why are finishes such as varnish applied to outdoor wooden furniture?
questions.solution: Varnish seals the surface, keeping out moisture to prevent rot, and makes the wood look better
questions.hint: Think about rain and sunshine on garden furniture

options: To protect the wood from moisture and decay and improve its appearance
To make the wood conduct electricity
To soften the wood for bending

questions.text: Which is a disadvantage of 3D printing for making many identical products?
questions.solution: 3D printing is ideal for prototypes and complex one-offs, but slow for large numbers of identical items
questions.hint: Think about the time it takes to build an item layer by layer

options: Each item is slow to print compared with injection moulding
A different mould is needed for every item
feedback: 3D printing is very good at complex shapes
3D printing does not use moulds

questions.text: Which process shapes metal by pouring it, molten, into a mould and leaving it to set? Give the process.
questions.solution: Casting pours molten metal into a mould; sand casting and die casting are types of casting
questions.hint: The same word is used for the actors chosen for a film

questions.text: A company uses CNC machines to make kitchen doors to each customer's own measurements. Which term describes this?
questions.solution: Mass customisation uses automated (CNC) production to make products tailored to each customer
questions.hint: It combines automated production with personal choices

feedback: Continuous production makes identical products non-stop

questions.text: What does 'ergonomics' mean in design?
questions.solution: Ergonomics is about how people interact with products: comfort, safety and ease of use
questions.hint: Think of a computer mouse shaped to fit the hand

options: Designing products so they are comfortable, safe and easy for people to use
Measuring the sizes of the human body
feedback: That is anthropometrics

questions.text: What is the term for the study of human body measurements used in design? Give the term.
questions.solution: Anthropometrics is the study of human body measurements, such as hand size or height
questions.hint: It begins with 'anthropo', meaning human

feedback.ergonomics: Ergonomics uses body data to make products easy to use; the measurements themselves are anthropometrics

questions.text: Which of the 6 Rs means using a product again, for the same or a different purpose?
questions.solution: Reuse means using a product again, such as a jam jar used for storage
questions.hint: Think of a glass jar used again to hold pens

feedback: Recycling breaks the material down to make something new

questions.text: Which designer created the London Underground map in 1931? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Harry Beck designed the Tube map in 1931, using straight lines and even spacing instead of true distances
questions.hint: His first name is Harry

questions.text: What is a design specification?
questions.solution: A specification lists the requirements (often measurable) that the product must meet
questions.hint: It is written after research and used to judge design ideas

options: A sketch of the final product
A short statement of the problem to be solved
A list of criteria that the product must meet
A record of tests on the finished product
feedback: That is a design brief

questions.text: Who designed the bagless cyclonic vacuum cleaner?
questions.solution: James Dyson developed the bagless cyclonic vacuum cleaner after making thousands of prototypes
questions.hint: The company that makes these cleaners has the designer's surname

feedback: Harry Beck designed the London Underground map
Issigonis designed the Mini car

questions.text: Which of the 6 Rs means not buying a product at all if it is not needed or is not sustainable? Give the word.
questions.solution: Refuse means saying no to products that are unnecessary or unsustainable
questions.hint: It means saying 'no thanks'

questions.text: Which statement about a design brief and a specification is accurate?
questions.solution: The brief is a short statement of the problem; the specification lists the requirements in detail
questions.hint: Which one comes first in the design process?

options: A brief states the problem; a specification lists the criteria the design must meet
A specification states the problem; a brief lists the criteria the design must meet
Both are final drawings of the product
A brief is written after the product is made
feedback: That is the wrong way round

questions.text: Which design approach puts the needs of the user at the centre of every stage and involves them in testing?
questions.solution: User-centred design involves users throughout, so the product meets their needs
questions.hint: The answer names the person who will use the product

feedback: Design fixation is getting stuck on one idea, which is a problem, not an approach

questions.text: Which designer created the original Mini car, launched in 1959?
questions.solution: Alec Issigonis designed the Mini, a small car with a lot of space inside for its size
questions.hint: He was a car engineer, not a furniture or product designer

feedback: Mackintosh was an Art Nouveau architect and furniture designer

questions.text: Which French designer created the Juicy Salif lemon squeezer? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Philippe Starck designed the Juicy Salif (1990) for Alessi
questions.hint: His first name is Philippe

questions.text: In a life cycle assessment (LCA), which stage comes first?
questions.solution: LCA follows a product from raw material extraction to manufacture, transport, use and disposal
questions.hint: Think about where the materials come from before anything is made

questions.text: What is the term for designing a product so that it will become out of date or stop working after a certain time? Give the term.
questions.solution: Planned obsolescence is designing a product to have a limited life so that people buy a replacement
questions.hint: The second word means 'becoming out of date'

questions.text: Which of the 6 Rs means mending a product rather than throwing it away?
questions.solution: Repair means fixing a product to make it last longer
questions.hint: Think about fixing a bike puncture

feedback: Recycling breaks the material down to make something new

questions.text: A chair seat height is chosen to suit people from the 5th to the 95th percentile. What data is the designer using?
questions.solution: Percentile tables of body measurements are anthropometric data
questions.hint: Percentiles describe human body measurements

feedback: Life cycle data is about environmental impact

questions.text: A phone's battery cannot be replaced and it stops getting software updates after a few years. Which term describes this?
questions.solution: Designing a product to have a limited useful life is planned obsolescence
questions.hint: The phone becomes out of date on purpose

questions.text: A designer makes a prototype, tests it with users, improves it and tests again several times. Which design strategy is this?
questions.solution: Iterative design is a cycle of prototyping, testing, evaluating and refining
questions.hint: 'Iterate' means to repeat

feedback: LCA measures environmental impact, not a design cycle

questions.text: A kettle handle is designed to fit the hand comfortably and keep the wrist straight when pouring. Which area of design is this?
questions.solution: Designing for comfort and ease of use is ergonomics
questions.hint: This area of design is about people using products comfortably

questions.text: Which Scottish designer is known for Art Nouveau furniture with tall ladder-back chairs and designed the Glasgow School of Art? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Charles Rennie Mackintosh designed the Glasgow School of Art and tall ladder-back chairs
questions.hint: His surname is also the name of a raincoat

questions.text: A product is broken down into its raw materials, which are then used to make new products. Which of the 6 Rs is this? Give the word.
questions.solution: Breaking a material down and making it into something new is recycling
questions.hint: Aluminium cans are melted down and made into new cans

feedback.reuse: Reusing keeps the product as it is; this breaks it down

questions.text: A specification point says: 'The torch must have a mass of less than 200 g.' Why is this a good specification point?
questions.solution: Good specification points are measurable, so the final product can be tested against them
questions.hint: How could you check whether the torch meets this point?

options: The point describes the colour of the torch
The point can be measured, so it can be tested
The point is only a personal opinion
The point names the manufacturing process

questions.text: Anthropometric data show seat heights from 400 mm (5th percentile) to 500 mm (95th percentile). Which design would suit 90% of users?
questions.solution: The 5th to 95th percentile covers 90% of users, so the seat must adjust across the whole range
questions.hint: The range from the 5th to the 95th percentile covers 90% of people

options: An adjustable seat from 400 mm to 500 mm
An adjustable seat from 300 mm to 400 mm

questions.text: Which product is linked with the Bauhaus and the designer Marcel Breuer?
questions.solution: Marcel Breuer designed the Wassily chair (1925) at the Bauhaus using bent tubular steel
questions.hint: Breuer was inspired by bicycle handlebars

options: The Wassily chair, made from tubular steel
feedback: The Red Blue Chair was designed by Gerrit Rietveld (De Stijl)

questions.text: Which statement about the 6 Rs is accurate?
questions.solution: Reduce means cutting down the materials and energy used in making and using a product
questions.hint: Check each definition carefully against the meaning of the word

options: Reduce means using fewer materials or less energy
Reuse means melting materials down to make new products
feedback: Mending is repair
That is recycling

questions.text: A life cycle assessment shows that most of a kettle's environmental impact happens while it is being used. Which change would reduce this impact the most?
questions.solution: If most impact is in use, saving energy during use (insulation, boiling only what is needed) makes the biggest difference
questions.hint: Focus on the stage of the life cycle with the biggest impact

options: Better insulation and a design that boils only the water needed
A new logo on the side

questions.text: Which De Stijl designer made the Red Blue Chair? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Gerrit Rietveld designed the Red Blue Chair (about 1918–1923), linked with De Stijl
questions.hint: His first name is Gerrit

questions.text: Which statement about anthropometrics and ergonomics is accurate?
questions.solution: Anthropometrics provides the body measurements; ergonomics uses them to make products comfortable and easy to use
questions.hint: One provides the data and the other uses it

options: Ergonomics is the measurement of body sizes
Anthropometrics is only about colour and style
Anthropometric data are used to make products ergonomic
They are exactly the same thing
feedback: Body measurements are anthropometrics

questions.text: A designer copies ideas from nature, such as burrs that inspired hook-and-loop fasteners. Give the term for this approach.
questions.solution: Biomimicry (biomimetics) copies solutions from nature, such as burrs inspiring hook-and-loop fasteners
questions.hint: 'Bio' means life and 'mimic' means copy

questions.text: Which statement about planned obsolescence is accurate?
questions.solution: Products designed to fail or date quickly are replaced sooner, increasing sales but also waste
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the old products

options: Planned obsolescence always makes products last longer
Planned obsolescence is a way of using recycled materials
Planned obsolescence can increase sales but creates more waste and uses more resources
feedback: Replacing products sooner increases waste

questions.text: Why is design for disassembly helpful for sustainability?
questions.solution: Products that are easy to take apart can be repaired and their materials separated for recycling
questions.hint: Think about what happens at the end of a product's life

options: Parts can be separated easily for repair, reuse or recycling
The product cannot be taken apart, so it is safer
The product is cheaper to advertise
The product is made from one material only

questions.text: Which statement about user-centred design is accurate?
questions.solution: In user-centred design, users are involved at every stage, from research to testing prototypes
questions.hint: Who is at the centre of this approach?

options: The designer works alone and shows users only the finished product
Users are consulted and involved in testing throughout, so the final product meets their needs
Only the cost of materials is considered
Products are designed to go out of date quickly
feedback: That is the opposite of user-centred design

questions.text: Which statement about Fairtrade is accurate?
questions.solution: The Fairtrade mark shows producers were paid a fair price and work in better conditions
questions.hint: Think about the people who grow the cotton or make the product

options: Fairtrade means a product is made from recycled materials
Fairtrade guarantees a product is organic
Fairtrade aims to give farmers and workers in developing countries a fair price and better conditions
Fairtrade is a British safety standard for toys

questions.text: A designer keeps producing ideas that are only small changes to their first idea. Which problem does this describe?
questions.solution: Design fixation is sticking too closely to one idea; strategies such as collaboration help avoid it
questions.hint: The designer is 'fixed' on one idea

feedback: Iterative design improves ideas through testing; it is not a problem

questions.text: Which German designer, who worked for Braun, is known for the phrase 'less, but better' and ten principles of good design? Give the surname.
questions.solution: Dieter Rams designed many Braun products and wrote ten principles of good design
questions.hint: His first name is Dieter

questions.text: Why do designers often use the 5th to 95th percentile range of anthropometric data?
questions.solution: Designing for every possible size is impractical; the 5th–95th percentile range suits 90% of people
questions.hint: Work out the percentage of people between the 5th and 95th percentiles

options: Designing for the extremes of everyone is impractical, so this range suits 90% of users
This range covers 100% of all users
This range includes only people aged 5 to 95
This range is the prices customers will pay
feedback: 5th to 95th percentile covers 90%, not 100%
